h1: Calling apps for HubSpot: Aircall vs Unitel Voice for small sales teams
dek: If your reps make calls and those calls never land on the HubSpot record, your pipeline report is fiction.
That's the filter for this page: two calling options for small sales teams that run HubSpot as the system of record.
disclosure: I earn a commission if you sign up through my link, at no extra cost to you. I only recommend tools I'd suggest anyway.

blocks.html: For a HubSpot sales or service team that needs calls on the contact and deal timeline, start with Aircall. It has a native HubSpot integration that logs calls and SMS to Contacts, Companies, Deals, and Tickets.

Unitel Voice is a simpler, cheaper business phone line. I could not confirm a HubSpot integration on Unitel's site. Fine for a solo founder who needs a business number. Weak fit if HubSpot call logging matters.
Pick the phone system by where the call record lives.

items: Small sales teams on HubSpot, such as SDRs, inbound desks, and founder-led outbound, that need shared numbers and call activity on the record.
Service teams that want tickets created from calls.
Not for: a team making a handful of personal calls a week that only needs a second line on a cell phone. Unitel can cover that. Aircall is more phone system than you need.

sections.label: What good looks like for a HubSpot dialer

items: Call activity on the right HubSpot objects (Contact, Company, Deal, Ticket).
Context before the answer: Insight Cards or the equivalent.
Call outcomes that can trigger HubSpot workflows, so follow-up isn't manual.

blocks.html: If the dialer can't do those three, you're buying a phone line, not a HubSpot calling layer.
Aircall is a cloud phone system for sales and support. On HubSpot, the useful part is the logging.

items: Calls and SMS log to Contacts, Companies, Deals, and Tickets, with duration, number, recording link, agent comments, outcomes, and transcription.
Insight Cards pull HubSpot context into the call screen before a rep answers.
Custom contact properties can trigger HubSpot workflows after a call.
Admins can auto-create tickets by call type.
Conversation Intelligence can bring transcription into HubSpot.

blocks.html: Plan gating: HubSpot's App Marketplace listing for Aircall says the integration requires an Aircall subscription on the Essentials or Professional plans, and the listing's Essentials card includes the HubSpot integration. Aircall's own pricing comparison lists the HubSpot integration on both of those plans.

items: Essentials: $30 per license per month, billed annually (vendor FAQ: annual billing is 25% off monthly). 3 licenses minimum on every plan.
Professional: $50 per license per month, billed annually. Adds Power Dialer, smart routing, queue callback, and conversation intelligence.
Enterprise: custom pricing, for teams of 25+ licenses.
Extra numbers: $6 per month for each extra number.
AI Voice Agents are also sold standalone from $99 per month minimum, separate from the dialer decision for most small teams.
Call data lands where HubSpot reporting and workflows already look.
Works for sales (deals) and service (tickets) in one account.
Power Dialer is there when you outgrow click-to-call (Professional).
Another subscription on top of HubSpot, with a 3-license minimum.
Someone has to own routing, properties, and ticket rules or it gets messy.
Overkill if you only need a personal business number.

blocks.html: Deeper write-up: Aircall for HubSpot teams.

sections.label: Unitel Voice: simple phone line, weak HubSpot fit

blocks.html: Unitel Voice gives you a toll-free or local business number that works on the phones you already carry, through its mobile app and desktop softphone. Auto attendant greetings, routing, and live US-based support. The Office plan adds desk phones and a dedicated account manager for setup.

items: Solo: $9.99 per month, or $84 billed yearly (1 user).
Team: $19.99 per month, or $168 billed yearly (unlimited users).
Office: $29.99 per month, or $252 billed yearly (3 users included), plus $7.99 per extra user per month.
30-day money-back guarantee.

blocks.html: HubSpot: I did not find a HubSpot integration on Unitel's site. Treat it as a standalone phone system. If HubSpot call logging is the job, look at Aircall instead of hoping a Zap will appear later.

items: Cheap, clear plans.
Works with phones you already carry.
Human support is the pitch, and Unitel leans into it.
No HubSpot sync I could confirm.
Not a sales-floor dialer.
Call recording is an add-on.
Need HubSpot call logging, Insight Cards, or workflow triggers from calls: Aircall (Essentials or Professional).
Need Power Dialer or outbound campaigns: Aircall Professional.
Need a business number only, and you'll live without automatic CRM logging: Unitel.
Before you buy either: decide which HubSpot objects get call activity and who owns the routing rules. Do that first. Then connect.

blocks.html: If your HubSpot contact data is already a mess, with duplicate numbers or wrong owners, fix that before you pipe a dialer into it.

faq.q: Do I need a dialer if HubSpot already has calling?
faq.a: HubSpot calling can be enough for light volume. A dedicated dialer matters when you need shared numbers, IVR, power dialing, or call analytics tied into workflows. Check what your HubSpot edition already includes before you buy.
